Insight 01 · Safety & reasoning foundations

AI Safety: Risks of General-Purpose AI (Keynote)

Yoshua Bengio (keynote) · International AI Safety Report
Goal

Map what general-purpose AI can do, the risks it brings, and the techniques that mitigate them.

Challenge

Capable, general models bring severe risks — loss of human control, decentralized misuse, and concentration of power.

Method
  • Synthesize evidence from ~100 experts across 30 countries (+ EU / UN / OECD)
  • Classify risks by source: misuse, human imitation, RL side-goals, reward hacking, self-preservation
  • Set safety requirements, e.g. never assert a false claim with confidence
Novelty

A shared, international evidence base for AI risk — not a single lab's opinion.

Impact

A common reference for governance and safe-deployment decisions as adoption rises.

[1] Y. Bengio et al., “International AI Safety Report,” IJCAI 2025 keynote.
Insight 02 · Safety & reasoning foundations

Graphical Models Meet Heuristic Search (Keynote) · Research Excellence Award

Rina Dechter (keynote) · UC Irvine
Goal

Solve hard reasoning and inference by combining probabilistic graphical models with heuristic search.

Challenge

Generic solvers struggle on very hard inference; pure search ignores the problem's structure.

Method
  • Find ‘tractable islands’ — subproblems you can solve exactly or efficiently
  • Use them as heuristics to guide search and Monte-Carlo sampling
  • Run anytime: a feasible result early, refined toward exact given more time
Novelty

The tractable-islands paradigm unifies exact inference, search, bounding and sampling.

Impact

Anytime solvers with guaranteed bounds — valuable when time or compute is limited.

[2] R. Dechter et al., “Graphical Models Meet Heuristic Search: A Personal Journey into Automated Reasoning,” IJCAI 2025 keynote.
Insight 03 · Explainability & robustness

Explainable Medical Reasoning with ILP

Dany Varghese et al. · University of Surrey, UK
Goal

Test whether Inductive Logic Programming can match black-box ML while staying interpretable.

Challenge

Medical AI is often accurate but a black box, which limits transparency and clinician trust.

Method
  • Learn symbolic if-then rules with the PyGol ILP system
  • Use Cleveland Heart Disease data (13 features, 303 patients) + medical background knowledge
  • Compare accuracy and global interpretability against standard ML
Novelty

Rule models reach comparable accuracy and align with real clinical logic — explainable by design.

Impact

For clinical adoption, transparent rules can matter more than marginal accuracy; points to neuro-symbolic hybrids.

[3] D. Varghese et al., “Explainable Medical Reasoning: From Data to Transparent, Trustworthy Clinical Insights,” IJCAI 2025.
Insight 04 · Explainability & robustness

Robust Compression Boundary for Embodied AI · Outstanding Paper

Chong Yu et al. · Fudan University
Goal

Compress embodied-AI models while keeping accuracy, efficiency AND robustness at once.

Challenge

On-device robots and vehicles need small, fast models that stay robust to real-world corruptions (noise, blur, weather).

Method
  • Characterize the ‘robust compression boundary’ — how far you can prune/quantize before robustness drops
  • Fold robustness constraints into the compression objective
  • Evaluate on embodied vision/robotics tasks vs accuracy-only baselines
Novelty

Treats robustness as a third axis alongside accuracy and efficiency, jointly optimized.

Impact

Lower memory/latency deployment on constrained platforms without losing robustness.

[4] C. Yu et al., “Boost Embodied AI Models with Robust Compression Boundary,” IJCAI 2025.
Insight 05 · Trustworthy & fair LLMs / MLLMs

Mitigating Linguistic Discrimination in LLMs

Guoliang Dong et al. · SMU & Zhejiang University
Goal

Measure and reduce how an LLM's safety and quality vary across languages.

Challenge

LLMs answer the same question differently by language — a safety- and knowledge-equity gap.

Method
  • Use metamorphic testing: same-meaning inputs in different languages should give same-meaning outputs
  • At inference, translate a query into k languages and answer each, then translate back
  • Pick the reply most consistent with the others by cosine similarity (voting)
Novelty

A translate-answer-vote wrapper that improves safety and quality with no retraining.

Impact

Lower jailbreak rates and higher F1 across languages — fairer, safer multilingual deployment.

[5] G. Dong et al., “Evaluating and Mitigating Linguistic Discrimination in Large Language Models,” IJCAI 2025.
Insight 06 · Trustworthy & fair LLMs / MLLMs

Modality-Fair Preference Optimization for MLLMs

Songtao Jiang et al. · Zhejiang University & NUS
Goal

Make multimodal LLMs rely fairly on both the image and the text.

Challenge

MLLMs often lean on text and under-use the image, which hurts trustworthiness.

Method
  • Perturb key image regions (text fixed) to build chosen vs rejected image pairs
  • Train a modality-fair loss aligning text and image preferences with a stability margin
  • Use keyword-guided region selection and easy-to-hard iterative training
Novelty

Balances preference alignment across modalities rather than text-only DPO.

Impact

Better-grounded, more trustworthy multimodal answers.

[6] S. Jiang et al., “Modality-Fair Preference Optimization for Trustworthy MLLM Alignment,” IJCAI 2025.
Insight 07 · Trustworthy & fair LLMs / MLLMs

Token-Level Accept or Reject: Micro Alignment

Yang Zhang et al. · Hong Kong Polytechnic University
Goal

Align an LLM without fine-tuning it — accept or reject each candidate token with a tiny model.

Challenge

RLHF/DPO fine-tune billions of parameters (costly) and align at the sentence level (coarse).

Method
  • Keep the LLM frozen; a small 3-layer accept/reject model filters each candidate token
  • Frame it as an MDP (accept/reject) with an alignment + divergence reward
  • Use top-k/top-p truncation for speed, with a fallback if all tokens are rejected
Novelty

Moves alignment from full fine-tuning to a lightweight, token-granular controller.

Impact

Much cheaper, more controllable alignment that retains or improves quality.

[7] Y. Zhang et al., “Token-Level Accept or Reject: A Micro Alignment Approach for Large Language Models,” IJCAI 2025.
Insight 08 · Trustworthy & fair LLMs / MLLMs

Hallucination Reduction in Video-Language Models

Jisheng Dang et al. · Lanzhou Univ., SYSU, NUS, HKU
Goal

Improve semantic alignment between video and text to cut hallucinations.

Challenge

Video-language models hallucinate when visual and language semantics are poorly aligned.

Method
  • Add a contrastive loss matching correct video-text pairs and separating mismatches
  • Two-stage training: broad video-language pre-training, then task fine-tuning
  • Inject text-semantic supervision into the visual Q-Former
Novelty

Hierarchical multimodal consistency makes visual features more semantically discriminative.

Impact

Fewer hallucinations and better video understanding for captioning and QA.

[8] J. Dang et al., “Hallucination Reduction in Video-Language Models via Hierarchical Multimodal Consistency,” IJCAI 2025.
Conclusions

Synthesis across the papers

Insights

  • Trustworthy AI is maturing — explainability need not cost accuracy (e.g. ILP rule models).
  • Robustness is emerging as a third design axis beyond accuracy and efficiency.
  • Lightweight alignment and fairness (token-level, modality-fair) work without full retraining.

Vision

  • A unified trust framework combining symbolic reasoning, probabilistic inference and neural learning.
  • AI agents with long-term memory, reasoning and self-monitoring.
  • More international AI governance around power concentration, bias and misuse.

Implications for us

  • Embed explainability and transparency modules into products.
  • Treat robustness-to-corruption as a first-class metric for embodied / edge AI.
  • Adopt cheap alignment (token-level, multilingual voting) for safer deployment.
